records.claim: The pipeline decode/rename stage provides the ROB index as a tag and clears the valid bit when an instruction writing a register is decoded.
records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit.
records.why: Section 4.2 describes the Tomasulo-like tracking table operation at decode.

records.claim: When an instruction completes execution, the payload is overwritten with the produced value digest and the valid bit is set.
records.quote: When the instruction completes, we overwrite the payload with the digest of the produced value and set the valid bit.
records.why: Section 4.2 defines the update of payload with the value digest and setting of the valid bit upon instruction completion.

records.claim: Whenever the branch predictor queries the table, entries with valid bit set forward their digests to register-value components in the SC.
records.quote: Whenever the branch predictor queries the table, any entry whose valid bit is set forwards its digest to the register-value components in the SC for prediction.
records.why: Section 4.2 describes query-time interface between the register status table and the SC.

records.claim: The total storage budget for the sR register component in the RUNLTS statistical corrector is 53,863 bits.
records.why: Table 3 specifies the exact storage breakdown and total of 53,863 bits for component sR.

records.claim: The register component tracks 65 logical registers across 8 banks (Bank 0 has 9 registers and Banks 1..7 have 8 registers).
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Section 4.2 establishes 8 banks each tracking 8 or 9 registers, and Table 3 confirms 65 registers.

records.claim: The legal parameter tuning range for NUM_LOGICAL_REGS is [32, 128].
records.open_question: The paper specifies a 65-register configuration (covering 64 architectural registers plus flag/condition register) but does not explore alternative logical register counts.

records.claim: Weights in both the prediction weight tables (WT) and usefulness tables (UT) are stored as 6-bit values.
records.why: Table 3 establishes that WT entries use 6 bits per weight, and UT entries use 6 bits per weight (6 x 65 x (2^3 + 2^3 + 2^3)).

records.claim: The legal parameter tuning range for WEIGHT_BITS is [4, 8].
records.open_question: The paper fixes weight counter width at 6 bits for all SC tables and does not explore alternative weight widths.

records.claim: The bank weight sum is fed into a multiplier stage that scales by 2.5 when selected.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL explicitly labels the multiplier stage as 'x0 or x2.5'.

records.claim: The legal parameter tuning range for USEFUL_MULTIPLIER is [1.0, 4.0].
records.open_question: The paper uses a fixed multiplier of 2.5 for sR and does not explore varying this scaling factor.

records.claim: The wire selecting x0 vs x2.5 in Figure 5(c) is controlled by bank usefulness rather than a global static scaling factor.
records.open_question: Declared ambiguity U2: Figure 5(c) does not label the wire selecting x0 vs x2.5. Bank usefulness is the natural driver by structural analogy to panels (a) and (b), but a global static scale of 2.5 cannot be ruled out from the figure alone.

records.claim: The 6-bit count of leading/trailing identical bits in integer register digests saturates at 63 rather than wrapping or counting bits matching the sign bit.
records.open_question: Declared ambiguity U3: Figure 6(a) allocates 6 bits to the count field for 64-bit registers (which can have 0..64 identical bits), leaving it unspecified whether the count saturates at 63, wraps modulo 64, or counts bits matching the sign bit.

records.claim: Usefulness tables in sR train when the bank prediction is correct rather than when the overall SC prediction is correct or when TAGE mispredicts but SC corrects.
records.open_question: Section 4.2 states that the register component comprises two tables (one tracking usefulness and one determining branch direction) and updates correlations for available registers, but does not state the exact mathematical condition under which usefulness counters are updated.

records.claim: On a branch misprediction squash, the Tomasulo-like table recovers by clearing entries matching squashed ROB tags rather than clearing all uncompleted entries or relying on lazy decay.
records.open_question: Section 5 explicitly notes that recovering the Tomasulo-like table on squashes presents challenges and is left for future work, leaving the exact pipeline squash recovery policy unspecified.

records.claim: At branch prediction lookup time, valid entries in the register status table forward their digests to the SC register-value components.
records.quote: Whenever the branch predictor queries the table, any entry whose valid bit is set forwards its digest to the register-value components in the SC for prediction.
records.why: Section 4.2 defines the prediction-time lookup trigger and forwarding from the register status table.

records.claim: The register component picks the digest of the most useful register among those available in each bank and forwards it to the second table.
records.quote: Unlike the existing components, this component picks the digest of the most useful register among those available and forwards it to the second table.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly describes picking the digest of the most useful register among available registers.

records.claim: Subscripts to per-bank usefulness tables UT0, UT1, UT2 must index by intra-bank register position (0..8) rather than absolute register identifier (0..64).
records.rejected: INCONSISTENT patch at a pointer no self-consistency check flagged

records.claim: A dedicated Tomasulo-like register status table contains one entry per logical register, consisting of a 1-bit valid bit, an 8-bit decay counter, and a 14-bit payload holding either a tag or a 12-bit digest.
records.quote: We use a dedicated table that contains one entry per logical register. Each entry consists of a valid bit and a payload that can hold either a 14-bit tag or a 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 describes the per-logical-register entries with valid bit, 14-bit tag, and 12-bit digest payload, and Table 3 lists { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65.

records.claim: Each entry of the usefulness table (UT) holds an eight- or nine-element vector of 6-bit weights reflecting the usefulness of each register in the bank.
records.quote: Each entry of the first table holds an eight- (or nine-) element vector of weights reflecting the usefulness of each register.
records.why: Section 4.2 specifies that UT entries hold an 8- or 9-element vector of weights per bank.

records.claim: Each bank contains three usefulness tables (UT0, UT1, UT2), each having 8 entries indexed by skewed PC hashes.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL explicitly identifies UT0, UT1, and UT2 with 8 entries each.

records.claim: The prediction weight tables (WT) are organized across 8 banks, each containing three tables: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), and WT2 (128 entries), storing 6-bit weights.
records.quote:
Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1",
    "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL explicitly details WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), and WT2 (128 entries) per bank, and Table 3 confirms 6-bit weights.

records.claim: The register component comprises two tables: one that tracks prediction usefulness and one that determines the predicted branch direction.
records.quote: As with the SC's existing components, it comprises two tables: one that tracks prediction usefulness and one that determines the predicted branch direction.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly establishes the two-table structure comprising usefulness tracking and direction prediction tables.

records.claim: The sR component is organized into exactly eight banks.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that the component is organized into eight banks.

records.claim: The legal parameter tuning range for NUM_BANKS is [4, 16] pow2.
records.open_question: The paper evaluates an 8-bank organization but does not explore other bank configurations.

records.claim: Prediction table WT0 contains 512 entries per bank.
records.quote:
Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1",
    "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL explicitly specifies 512 entries for WT0.

records.claim: The legal parameter tuning range for WT0_ENTRIES is [128, 2048] pow2.
records.open_question: The paper fixes WT0 at 512 entries per bank and does not explore alternative entry counts.

records.claim: Prediction table WT1 contains 256 entries per bank.
records.quote:
Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1",
    "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL explicitly specifies 256 entries for WT1.

records.claim: The legal parameter tuning range for WT1_ENTRIES is [64, 1024] pow2.
records.open_question: The paper fixes WT1 at 256 entries per bank and does not explore alternative entry counts.

records.claim: Prediction table WT2 contains 128 entries per bank.
records.quote:
Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1",
    "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL explicitly specifies 128 entries for WT2.

records.claim: The legal parameter tuning range for WT2_ENTRIES is [32, 512] pow2.
records.open_question: The paper fixes WT2 at 128 entries per bank and does not explore alternative entry counts.

records.claim: Each usefulness table (UT0, UT1, UT2) contains 8 entries per bank.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL explicitly specifies 8 entries for each usefulness table.

records.claim: The legal parameter tuning range for UT_ENTRIES is [4, 64] pow2.
records.open_question: The paper fixes each UT table at 8 entries and does not explore alternative table sizes.

records.claim: The register digest size is 12 bits.
records.quote: RUNLTS generates a 12-bit digest from each 64-bit register value, with the format depending on the register type.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6 explicitly specify a 12-bit digest for register values.

records.claim: The legal parameter tuning range for DIGEST_BITS is [8, 16].
records.open_question: The paper fixes the register digest width at 12 bits and does not explore alternative digest widths.

records.claim: For integer registers, the 12-bit digest encodes the count of leading zeros/ones, trailing zeros/ones, and the 6 least significant bits.
records.quote: For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits, effectively capturing characteristics of addresses and round numbers.
records.why: Section 4.2 specifies the three components of the integer register digest.

records.claim: For condition-code flags, the four flag bits are replicated three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.quote: For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly defines replicating the 4 condition-code flag bits three times to create the 12-bit digest.

records.claim: For floating-point registers, format classification inspects the MSBs and extracts the sign bit along with the most significant bits of the exponent.
records.quote: For floating-point registers, we inspect the most significant bits to classify the format and then extract the sign bit along with the most significant bits of the exponent.
records.why: Section 4.2 specifies inspecting the MSBs to classify the floating-point format and extracting the sign bit and exponent MSBs.

records.claim: To prevent stale digests from polluting the predictor, each digest entry is invalidated 256 decoded instructions after the producing instruction was decoded.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly establishes the 256-decoded-instruction threshold for digest invalidation.

records.claim: The bank prediction sum is multiplied by 2.5 if bank usefulness is positive, and gated to x0 otherwise.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL explicitly defines the 'x0 or x2.5' multiplier stage at the output of the bank WT sum.

records.claim: If several registers were available within the same bank at prediction time, the update algorithm randomly selects one of them for training.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update. Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly defines the random selection rule among available registers per bank during update.
